Cloverdale
tags.note: Cloverdale, officially named a community in 1982, was named by railway engineers after Clover Valley, an area settled by William Shannon in 1875. Post Office opened 1892; station c.1891. Now part of Surrey’s municipal boundary.

tags.name: Elgin
tags.note: Elgin, officially named 3 July 1952, was settled by 1879. Named in 1885 by W.C. McDougall after Lord Elgin, Canada’s governor-general (1847–55). The Elgin Post Office operated from 1885 to 1909.

tags.name: Cassin
tags.note: Cassin Station, officially named 15 September 1966, was previously identified as Pipe Line Station in CP timetables until 1963. Located 3 miles east of Port Moody, it appears as a community or urban community on maps from 1981 onward.

tags.name: Douglas
tags.note: Douglas, at the Peace Arch border crossing, was named for pioneer Benjamin Douglas, who laid out the townsite in 1889. Officially adopted 1957; site commemorates the 1846 Oregon Treaty between Britain and the US.

tags.name: Fern Ridge
tags.note: Fern Ridge, officially named 1951, is a community in Langley, BC. Its post office operated from 1908 to 1926, serving local residents from a location in Section 23, Township 7, west of the 6th Meridian.

tags.name: Brookswood
tags.note: Brookswood, officially named 1951, is a community in Langley, BC. Its post office operated from 1925 to 1926 on Lot 20, Section 35, Township 7, serving the early local settlement.

tags.name: White Rock
tags.note: White Rock, named for a large white boulder on its beach, was first a Great Northern Railway station. Post Office opened 1910; incorporated as a city in 1957. Name linked to Coast Salish legend.
